skill.name: writing-fragments
skill.description: Guided interview for collecting writing fragments into a single markdown file. Use it when the user wants raw material, early ideas, claims, vignettes, or sharp sentences before outlining.
skill.summary: Captures unstructured writing fragments in one markdown document before drafting.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The two external command findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences in the file format example. The system reconnaissance finding is also a false positive because the skill asks the user for a save path and does not enumerate system information.

static_findings.snippet: If the user did not pass a path, ask once where to save the document, then remember it for the rest

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 40 opens a fenced markdown example and does not execute shell or Ruby code. The surrounding lines describe the output file format only.
Line 63 closes the same fenced markdown example and has no executable behavior. There is no instruction to run commands or pass user input to a shell.
The line asks the user where to save the document when no path was provided. It does not request host details, enumerate files, or collect system information.

content.value_statement: Writers often lose useful thoughts before a draft has structure. This skill interviews you, captures fragments, and appends them to one markdown document.
actual_capabilities: Interviews the user to surface claims, scenes, quotes, and half-formed ideas.
Appends fragments to a single markdown file during the session.
Uses one H1 title and separates fragments with horizontal rules.
Re-reads the file before each write to preserve user edits.
Supports user requests to cut, rewrite, or merge recent fragments.
limitations: Does not create outlines, article structure, metadata, or tables of contents.
Requires a user-provided save path when no path is given.
Works only within files the active AI tool can read and write.
Does not fact-check or publish the final article.

use_cases.title: Explore an Essay Idea
use_cases.description: A writer can talk through a topic while useful sentences and claims are captured as raw material.

use_cases.title: Collect Product Narrative Notes
use_cases.description: A product lead can record customer stories, objections, and concise claims before shaping a launch draft.

use_cases.title: Preserve Research Impressions
use_cases.description: A researcher can capture observations and quotes while keeping them separate from a formal outline.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Fragment File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-fragments. I want to write about [topic]. Save the file at [path]. Ask me questions and capture useful fragments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a new writing session with a clear topic and save path.

prompt_templates.title: Develop Raw Material
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-fragments with [path]. Interview me about [topic] and append claims, examples, and sharp sentences as they appear.
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a larger pool of fragments from an early idea.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Recent Fragments
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-fragments with [path]. Re-read the file, ask targeted questions about [angle], and append sharper fragments without adding an outline.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve the quality of new fragments while keeping the file unstructured.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Deep Interview
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-fragments with [path]. Challenge my assumptions about [topic], capture contradictions, and preserve any phrases that may survive into the final essay.
prompt_templates.scenario: Probe a complex topic and collect stronger raw material.

output_examples.input: I want to write about why developer tools feel slower than they should.
output_examples.output: The skill adds a working title and several fragments, including a latency claim, a short vignette, and a sharper sentence.

output_examples.input: The last idea is too soft. Make it more direct.
output_examples.output: The relevant fragment is rewritten with firmer language, while the rest of the file is preserved.

best_practices: Provide a clear file path at the start of the session.
Keep talking in natural language and let the skill decide what becomes a fragment.
Review the file during the session and ask for cuts, rewrites, or merges when needed.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to produce a full outline before gathering fragments.
Do not use it as a fact-checking or citation tool.
Do not store secrets, private credentials, or restricted personal data in the fragment file.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a markdown document filled with raw writing fragments for a future article or essay.

faq.question: Does it write the final article?
faq.answer: No. It collects raw material before structure, outlining, and final drafting.

faq.question: Can I edit the file during the session?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill re-reads the file before each write so your edits are preserved.

faq.question: What counts as a fragment?
faq.answer: A fragment can be a claim, scene, quote, sentence, complaint, example, or half-formed thought.

faq.question: Does it need file access?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude, Codex, or Claude Code must be able to read and write the selected markdown file.

faq.question: Can it organize fragments into sections?
faq.answer: No. The skill keeps fragments unstructured unless you ask for a specific local edit.
